tier1.text: The obturator internus turns the thigh outward at the hip. This turn, called lateral rotation, moves the front of the thigh away from the body's midline. Each obturator internus covers most of the side wall of the pelvis. The obturator internus lies deeper than the gluteus maximus, the largest buttock muscle.
